commitResults.messageTitle: Update README with new features and examples
commitResults.messageBody:
Add README docs for find, persistence, exit

The README previously only documented features 1-3 (add, list,
delete). Features 4-6 (find, automatic data persistence, exit)
were implemented but undocumented, leaving users without guidance
on how to search records or what happens to their data between
sessions.

Document the find command's syntax and matching behaviour, explain
that persistence is automatic with no user action required, and
describe the exit command, following the same format already used
for features 1-3.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix heading level for features 4-6 in README
commitResults.messageBody:
Features 4-6 (find, persistence, exit) were added as H2 headings
instead of H3, causing them to render with an underline that
doesn't match the H3 styling used by features 1-3.

Change the three headings from ## to ### to match the existing
heading hierarchy.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add user stories 17-32 to Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The User stories table only had stories for extension-style and
nice-to-have behaviour (undo, shortcuts, anomaly detection, etc.).
None of the core CRUD commands - add, list, delete, find, automatic
persistence, exit - had a story, and the table ended with a
"{More to be added}" placeholder for the second half of the
assigned stories.

Add 14 stories covering the missing core commands as must-haves,
plus should-have and nice-to-have stories for filtering, team
roster views, sorting, leave-status lookup, delete confirmation,
and workforce-connectivity checks, following the same Priority /
As a / I can / So that I can format already used in the table.

These fill out the "17-32" half of the user stories assigned in
Week 7, matching priorities to what's actually implemented versus
still planned, per the course's requirement that the DG cover the
full product scope rather than just the current iteration.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add id, department and role to Employee
commitResults.messageBody:
Give Employee the fields from the feature spec: employee ID, name,
phone, email, department and role. Remove address and remark, along
with the tutorial's remark command, since HuntR does not use them.

Identify employees by their employee ID instead of their name. IDs
are 1 to 20 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores and are compared
case-insensitively, so company-specific ID schemes are supported.
Department and role accept common punctuation such as "R&D".

Update the add and edit commands, storage, UI card, sample data and
tests for the new fields. Employee IDs cannot be edited.

Tags are not part of the agreed HuntR employee fields or of the add,
list and delete outputs, so remove them: the t/ option of add and
edit, the tags shown on the employee card and in command messages,
and their storage.

Also delete src/main/java/seedu/address/model/util/92624417, a
duplicate of SampleDataUtil that was added by mistake.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add employee rules for names, duplicates and errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Make the add command follow the feature spec and the Week 8 guidance.

Names may contain relation words such as s/o, d/o and a/l, as well as
hyphens, apostrophes and non-Latin letters. Words like d/o are treated
as part of the name instead of the department prefix. Extra spaces in
names are collapsed.

Reject an employee whose ID already exists with the spec's message.
Add an employee whose name only differs in case or spacing from an
existing one, but warn the user so a duplicate can be spotted.

Accept more phone layouts, such as +65 6123-4567 and labels in
brackets. Reject unknown parameters, and give separate error messages
for blank, too long, too few digits and invalid characters.
Implement exit command
Implement find employees by name

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix name, phone and department parsing edge cases
commitResults.messageBody:
Only treat relation words such as d/o and s/o as part of a name when
they appear inside the name field. A department such as "O & G" that
follows other fields was wrongly read as name text.

Accept combining marks in names, so names such as the Tamil name
written with a virama and an accent stored as a separate character
are valid. Store names in their standard Unicode form so that both
spellings are the same name, including in the similar-name warning.

Check phone numbers with a loop instead of a regular expression. The
regular expression overflowed the stack on very long input.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use employee ID to select employee in edit command
commitResults.messageBody:
The edit command identifies the target employee by its index in the
displayed list, while delete is moving to employee IDs. Using different
ways to pick an employee for the two commands is confusing.

Let's make edit take id/EMPLOYEE_ID instead:

* Parse a required id/ prefix in EditCommandParser and reject any
  preamble, such as an index.
* Look up the employee in the full employee list, so employees hidden
  by a find filter can still be edited.
* Report "No employee with ID X was found." when no employee matches.

The employee ID itself is still not editable.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix failing delete parser test for too-long IDs
commitResults.messageBody:
DeleteCommandParserTest expects the general employee ID constraint
message for a 21-character ID. However, ParserUtil#parseEmployeeId now
reports a more specific message when an ID is valid apart from its
length, so the test fails on master.

Let's keep the more specific message, and test the too-long ID
separately against it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share name relation word and unknown parameter handling with edit
commitResults.messageBody:
The edit command reads "d/o" in a name such as "Nur Aisha d/o Ali" as
the department prefix, silently splitting the name. It also folds
unknown parameters such as x/foo into the previous value. The add
command already handles both cases, but its logic is private to
AddCommandParser.

Let's move that logic into a package-private ArgumentPreprocessor
class, and use it from both AddCommandParser and EditCommandParser.
Relation words are still only treated as name text inside the name
field, so "d/O & G" after another field is read as a department.

error separately so users can correct the relevant problem.

documentation outside this change.
